evidence: Prompts for a hidden password under the System Preferences title and retries dscl authonly until it authenticates. The password is only used for verification in these bytes; it is not saved or replayed to sudo.
Reads Chrome Safe Storage using security find-generic-password, writes the result into /tmp/osalogging/storage.txt and copies Keychain databases, ~/.aws and ~/.ssh into the staging directory.

If Trezor Suite is installed, downloads and unzips remote resources, overwrites its app.asar and Info.plist, ad-hoc signs the app and clears all extended attributes. It does not launch the modified wallet.
Creates /tmp/osalogging.zip with ditto and PUTs that exact file to a remote /gate endpoint.
samples.limits: This is source reconstruction, not an authenticated original binary. Downloaded wallet resources were not supplied. No runtime success is asserted: a failed shell command, absent credential directory, cancelled dialog or filesystem permissions can stop this unguarded script. No privilege escalation, browser-cookie reading or password database decryption is present.
samples.coverage: Four hostile findings cover password phishing, validated multistore acquisition, wallet resource replacement and multistore archive export; three new suspicious traits describe individual sensitive store copies.

samples.identification: Loopback OAuth command-injection PoC with dynamic-registration stub
evidence: HTTPServer is bound only to 127.0.0.1:8765. Unrecognized GETs and token POSTs return the OAuth resource_metadata challenge.

Discovery advertises https://evil.test/$([IO.File]::WriteAllText(...)) with a fixed C:\Users\Public\pwned.txt / RCE marker. Python serves the string; a vulnerable shell-based client opener would have to evaluate it.
POST /register reads and discards the body and returns the constant local-poc-client identifier. There is no credential storage, token issuance, exfiltration, persistence or remote control.
samples.limits: No original repository, authorized-test statement, target client or deployment history was supplied. The loopback binding, reserved test host and single fixed proof marker favor a local regression/reproduction tool. Deliberate use against a victim would change the deployment assessment, not the payload detections.
samples.finding_review: All four hostile/suspicious exploit findings are accurate and retained; a BENIGN artifact verdict does not erase the injected command technique.

evidence: Same loopback binding, challenge/discovery sequence and fixed PowerShell file-write marker as the registration variant.

samples.limits: Same missing origin and deployment context as the registration variant; a vulnerable external client is required for the embedded command to execute.
